newsitem.title: USA: Tupperware sees slightly lower Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: Tupperware sees slightly lower Q1 net.

text.p: Tupperware Corp said on Monday that it expects lower first quarter net income compared with last year based on lower than expected sales and the impact of unfavorable foreign exchange.
"We are disappointed to report a softer than expected outlook for March, our key month in the quarter," Warren Batts, Tupperware chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement.
Tupperware said its second quarter earnings may also be slightly lower despite increased sales, compared with the year ago period.

The soft first half results prompted the company to cut its 1997 target for a mid-single digit sales increase and slight growth in net income versus last year's $176.0 million proforma net income, Tupperware said.
A strong performance in the European market does not appear to offset weakness elsewhere, Tupperware said.

First quarter Asia Pacific sales are expected to be down in the low double-digit range and profits are expected to be down significantly due to a difficult comparison, as well as continuing softness in Japan and the Philippines, Tupperware said.
The U.S. sales decline has not moderated as expected -- leading to a higher operating loss in the region when combined with higher costs, Tupperware said.
Latin America also faces a difficult comparison, as well as lower productivity after a strong finish to 1996, the company said.

Similar conditions are expected to affect the United States and Asia Pacific operations in the second quarter, the company said. Second quarter Latin American results are expected to return to double-digit growth, Tupperware said.
Europe will have a difficult comparison in the second quarter, but the target is slight improvement, the company said.
Tupperware's 1996 net income excluded $9.1 million in pretax costs associated with its May 1996 spin off from Premark International Inc.
Tupperware reported proforma 1996 operating earnings per share of $0.46 in the first quarter, $0.77 a share in the second and $2.79 for the year.

Analysts had expected the company to earn $0.51 a share in the first quarter, $0.86 a share in the second quarter and $3.05 a share for the year, according to First Call's consensus of analysts' earnings estimates.
